newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kansai Electric awards contracts to buy power.
newsitem.headline: Kansai Electric awards contracts to buy power.

text.p: Kansai Electric Power Co Inc said on Tuesday that it had signed formal contracts to purchase up to about 1.12 million kilowatts (kw) of electricity from four companies under two schemes.

The electric utility said in a statement that it has awarded contracts to Kobe Steel Ltd, Nippon Steel Corp and Nakayama Kyodo Hatsuden -- a subsidiary of Nakayama Steel Works Ltd -- to purchase a total of 323,500 kw in a contract starting in 1999.
It will also purchase a total of 799,000 kw from Osaka Gas and Kobe Steel under a contract starting in 2002.
Kobe Steel has said it would spend about 158 billion yen to build power-generating facilities to supply electricity to Kansai Electric.
It said in a statement that the new facilities would be built at the company's complexes in Kobe and Kakogawa, both in Hyogo prefecture, western Japan.
Kansai Electric also said that it will issue a tender during the fiscal year starting on April 1 to purchase a total of about 700,000 kw from 2004.
